EngLawName: Special Act for Post-Disaster Reconstruction of the Matai'an River Landslide Dam in Hualien
name: 花蓮馬太鞍溪堰塞湖災後重建特別條例

articles.content:
This Act is enacted to ensure the efficient,  swift implementation of the recovery and reconstruction work in the Matai'an River Landslide Dam disaster affected areas in Hualien.
  Matters not stipulated in this Act, the provisions of the Disaster Prevention and Protection Act and other relevant laws shall apply. However, where other laws provide provisions more favorable to post-disaster  recovery,  reconstruction, and remediation, the most advantageous provisions shall apply.
  Where the reconstruction areas are located within Indigenous tribe, the relevant provisions of the Indigenous Peoples Basic Law shall apply.
The disaster affected areas under this Act refer to the areas affected by the Matai'an River Landslide Dam in Hualien, the scope of which shall be publicly announced by the Executive Yuan.

The competent authority under this Act shall be the Public Construction Commission, Executive Yuan.
  The central implementing authority under this Act shall be the respective central authority in charge of the relevant affairs; the local implementing authority shall be the Hualien County Government.

The scope of post-disaster recovery, reconstruction, and remediation projects under this Act shall include the following categories:
1.The follow-up handling of the remediation of the Matai'an River Landslide Dam shall be supervised by the Executive Yuan and planned, prevented, and implemented by the Public Construction Commission, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the Hualien County Government. Relevant engineering projects shall include disaster reduction, monitoring, evacuation, and strategy for dam breaches, as well as reinforcement and elevation of embankments.
2.Agricultural Recovery:
(1)Excavation, removal and disposal of earth and rock from farmland, soil replacement, farmland restoration, designated fallow programs, reconstruction of abandoned farmland, farmland readjustment, and reconstruction of the agricultural production environment.
(2)Farm roads, forest roads, and agricultural transportation facilities.
(3)Greenhouses, net houses, storage facilities, livestock and poultry barns, rendering plants, composting facilities, supply sheds, and agricultural machinery rooms.
(4)Facilities and equipment for crop replanting and seedling planting.
(5)Agricultural machinery and equipment.
(6)Fishing harbors, fishing boats, and aquaculture facilities.
3.Power systems:
(1)Substations and transmission lines above ultra-high voltage.
(2)Disaster resilience of the distribution networks.
(3)Streetlights and public lighting facilities.
(4)Emergency backup power systems, mobile power supply, self-generated power supply and energy storage and other micro-grid facilities.
4.Telecommunications systems and cable radio and television systems:
(1)Public telecommunications networks.
(2)Mobile communication base station vehicles.
(3)Satellite communication backup facilities.
(4)Cable radio and television systems.
5.Tap water, gas, and fuel facilities:
(1)Tap water and simplified water supply equipment.
(2)Gas and fuel pipelines.
6.Housing and public facilities:
(1)Subsidies and rental assistance for disaster-damaged and irreparably destroyed buildings and residences, including desilting, demolition, repairs, and reconstruction either on-site or at an alternative location.
(2)Demolition, clearance, and restoration of facilities and equipment belonging to public buildings, schools, kindergartens, government agencies or institutions, and social welfare organizations.
(3)Emergency repairs and restoration of cultural assets and indigenous cultural health stations  and gathering places.
(4)Establishment of interactive public and household alarm systems.
(5)Restoration of religious buildings such as temples, churches, and chapels.
(6)Support for home cleanup and consolation payments for recovery.
7.Hydraulic facilities:
(1)Systematic management of upstream, midstream, and downstream river and drainage systems, agricultural irrigation and drainage systems, coastal protection facilities.
(2)Stormwater and sanitary sewers and road drainage.
(3)Slopeland remediation and debris flow control.
(4)Runoff allocation, outflow control, and on-site flood retention measures.
(5)Post-disaster recovery and reconstruction works for rivers and drainage facilities administered by central government and   county (city) governments, and reconstruction of bridges across rivers and drainage bottlenecks.
8.Roads and transportation:
(1)Roads, bridges and tunnels.
(2)Road slope protection and bank protection works.
(3)Traffic signals, signs, guardrails and other ancillary works and facilities.
9.Environmental sanitation recovery:
(1)Post-disaster waste clearance and disposal, repair and reconstruction of environmental protection facilities, and environmental recovery.
(2)Post-disaster disease prevention and treatment.
10.Social recovery and industrial promotion:
(1)Disaster relief, psychological counseling, and social support.
(2)Post-disaster recovery measures such as local industry revitalization, subsidies for business equipment, and low-interest loans.
(3)Revitalization of cultural tourism, leisure agriculture, and cultural industry.
(4)Recovery measures such as cash relief for agriculture natural disasters and interest subsidies for low-interest loans.
(5)Disaster victim assistance, replacement of production equipment, restoration of industrial facilities, business equipment, transportation, various assistive devices, and vehicles.
11.Other projects deemed necessary for recovery and reconstruction by the respective central implementing authorities.
  The qualifications, criteria, subsidy amounts, required documentation, matters that may be delegated, commissioned, or entrusted, and other related matters for granting allowances, subsidies, relief payments, consolation payments, wages, and other forms of compensation for the recovery and reconstruction projects set forth in the preceding paragraph, shall be formulated by the respective central implementing authorities.

Assistance for households affected by flooding shall be based on the actual number of affected households, and shall not be restricted by the limitation of one household per house number. The regulatory restrictions under the current Categories and Standards of Assistance in Flood Disaster shall not apply.

Post-disaster reconstruction in the affected areas shall respect the people, communities, tribes, organizations, cultures, and lifestyles of the region.
  To resettle disaster-affected people or carry out reconstruction in the disaster-affected areas, all levels of government may simplify administrative procedures regarding the designation, acquisition, modification, evaluation, management, maintenance, or other matters related to land and buildings, and apply Article 40 of the Disaster Prevention and Protection Act.

The funding required under this Act shall be capped at NT$30 billion, and relevant plans may be formulated and special budgets may be prepared in phases in light of changes in circumstances; the preparation and implementation of such budgets shall not be subject to the restrictions stipulated in Article 23, Article 62, and Article 63 of the Budget Act.
  The sources of the funding required under the preceding paragraph may be financed by reallocating surplus from previous years or by borrowing; the annual borrowing limit each year shall not be subject to the restrictions stipulated in Article 5, Paragraph 7 of the Public Debt Act. The total borrowing limit for the general budget and special budget of the central government during the implementation period of this Act shall not exceed 15% of the total annual expenditures of the general budgets and special budgets of the central government for the same period.
  During the implementation period of this Act, the budgeted outstanding balance of public debts borrowed by the central government for more than one year shall be handled in accordance with Article 5, Paragraph 1 of the Public Debt Act.
  The central government may provide subsidies upon verification for the funds required by local implementing authority to carry out the matters under this Act and the Disaster Prevention and Protection Act. The central implementing authorities may also agree that the local governments receiving the subsidies may implement them through a collection and payment arrangement.
  To meet the urgent needs of disaster relief and recovery and reconstruction work in disaster affected areas, the central implementing authorities may, after reporting to and obtaining the approval of the Executive Yuan, make partial payments prior to the completion of statutory procedures for the special budget referred to in the first paragraph.
  Funds subsidized by the central government to the local implementing authority shall be used by the local implementing authority in accordance with the purpose and projects of the subsidy and shall not be diverted for other uses.

Where any disaster affected areas under this Act is not within the scope of disaster affected areas announced in accordance with Article 51 of the Disaster Prevention and Protection Act, the provisions of that Act relating to disaster affected areas shall apply mutatis mutandis to the recovery and reconstruction.

Allowances, subsidies, relief payments, consolation payments, and other forms of compensation received from the respective implementing authorities in accordance with this Act shall be exempt from income tax.
  Allowances, subsidies, relief payments, consolation payments, and other forms of compensation received from the respective implementing authorities in accordance with this Act shall not be subject to offset, seizure, security, or compulsory enforcement.

The central government ministries and agencies that prepare budgets in accordance with this Act shall submit post-disaster recovery and reconstruction plans within two months following the enforcement of this Act.
  The central government ministries and agencies that prepare budgets in accordance with this Act shall submit to the Legislative Yuan for reference, on a quarterly basis, a summary of the implementation of the work plans and the estimated progress associated with the budget.

The competent authority shall establish a dedicated section on its information website to provide complete information that can be easily searched and can be understood, and proactively disclose the following implementation progress and content under this Act on a regular monthly basis:
1.Announcement of the disaster affected areas pursuant to Article 2.
2.Regulations formulated by each central implementing authority pursuant to Article 4, Paragraph 2.
3.The contents as stipulated in the preceding Article.

The implementation period of this Act and its special budget shall commence from the date of promulgation until March 31, 2027. However, the provisions stipulated in Subparagraph 1, Subparagraph 2 Item 1, and Subparagraph 7 Items 1 to 3 of Paragraph 1 of Article 4 shall remain in effect until December 31, 2030.
  Upon expiration of the implementation period of this Act and its special budget, an extension may be granted with the consent of the Legislative Yuan.
